message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the ancestor of the clade that includes all **Laurasiatheria**—the group that contains the orders Carnivora (lions), Perissodactyla (zebras), Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, Pholidota, Scandentia, and Tubulidentata. In other words, the two species share a common ancestor that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, when the Laurasiatherian lineage split from other placental mammals.
